introduction: Two young friends leave Verona for courtly life, carrying different ideas about love, loyalty and the uses of travel. Valentine expects experience abroad to improve him, while Proteus initially places his devotion to Julia above worldly opportunity. At the Duke's court, Silvia's affection and her father's marriage plans expose the friends to competing desires. Letters, exchanged tokens and a woman's disguise test whether declarations can be trusted, while the servants' jokes and a troublesome dog place lofty promises beside everyday acts of care.

fullSynopsis.text: Valentine leaves Verona for Milan, mocking his friend Proteus's absorption in love. Proteus remains devoted to Julia, who pretends to reject his letter before privately cherishing its torn pieces. His father Antonio decides that travel and courtly experience will improve him. When Proteus conceals Julia's letter by claiming it comes from Valentine, his own excuse reinforces the decision to send him away. He and Julia exchange rings and promises of constancy before parting.

In Milan, Valentine has fallen in love with Silvia, the Duke's daughter, and become the kind of lover he formerly ridiculed. His servant Speed explains Silvia's playful device of making him write a love letter to himself. The Duke favours the wealthy Thurio, whom Silvia dislikes, but she and Valentine have agreed to marry and escape by a rope ladder from her window. Valentine welcomes Proteus and trusts him with the plan. Proteus immediately desires Silvia, and deliberately resolves to betray both his friend and Julia in pursuit of her.

Julia, still trusting Proteus, persuades Lucetta to prepare a page's disguise so that she can travel to him with less danger from predatory men. Proteus's servant Lance supplies another account of loyalty through his attachment to the unresponsive dog Crab, dramatising his family's farewell and later recounting punishments accepted for the animal's offences. Lance and Speed also debate a prospective milkmaid bride's virtues, faults and wealth. Their practical talk of love and service accompanies their masters' elaborate professions and disguises.

Proteus reveals the intended elopement to the Duke while pretending that duty has overcome friendship. The Duke tricks Valentine into exposing the concealed ladder and a letter to Silvia, then banishes him under threat of death. Proteus offers the devastated Valentine apparent comfort and help with future correspondence. The Duke next employs Proteus to turn Silvia against Valentine and towards Thurio, trusting his supposed fidelity to Julia. Proteus uses that access to press his own suit. Outside the city, outlaws intercept Valentine and choose him as their captain; he accepts on condition that they spare vulnerable women and poor travellers.

Arriving in male disguise as Sebastian, Julia hears Proteus serenade Silvia and falsely claim that Julia is dead. Silvia condemns his broken promises and remains faithful to Valentine. Proteus then hires the disguised Julia and sends her to Silvia with Julia's own ring, a letter and a request for a portrait. Silvia tears the letter, refuses to wrong Julia by accepting her ring, and gives the supposed page money out of sympathy for his abandoned mistress. Her kindness tempers Julia's jealousy. Silvia separately enlists Eglamour to help her escape an enforced marriage and find Valentine.

Silvia flees with Eglamour, but outlaws capture her while he runs away. The Duke, Thurio, Proteus and Julia follow into the forest. Proteus claims to have rescued Silvia from the outlaws and demands her affection as his reward. When she rejects him, he seizes her and threatens sexual force. Valentine emerges from concealment and stops him, denouncing the betrayal. Proteus asks forgiveness, which Valentine grants at once, declaring that he gives Proteus all that was his in Silvia. Silvia makes no further speech; Julia swoons at the offer.

Julia's handling of the exchanged rings reveals her identity. She rebukes Proteus's inconstancy, and he turns back towards her; both declare that their wishes are fulfilled. Outlaws bring in the Duke and Thurio. Valentine threatens Thurio, who abandons his claim to Silvia rather than risk his life. The Duke now approves Valentine, recalls him from banishment and grants Silvia to him. At Valentine's request he also pardons the outlaws. The company prepares to return for celebrations, and Valentine proposes that the two couples share a wedding day. The reconciliation leaves Silvia's response to the men's settlement unspoken and the marriages still ahead.

acts.label: ACT I
acts.summary: Valentine departs for Milan, treating Proteus's devotion to Julia as a waste of youthful opportunity. Proteus sends her a letter through Speed, whose account of the delivery confuses him. Julia discusses suitors with Lucetta and affects anger at the letter, tearing it before privately kissing and gathering its fragments. Antonio, persuaded that his son needs experience abroad, resolves to send Proteus to join Valentine. Proteus hides Julia's reply by pretending it describes his friend's successful courtly life. That fiction makes Antonio still more determined that he leave immediately. Proteus recognises that his attempt to protect his love has instead hastened their separation, but cannot reverse his father's order.

acts.label: ACT II
acts.summary: Speed teases Valentine about his transformation into a lover and explains that Silvia's request for a letter was a means of declaring her affection for its writer. Proteus and Julia exchange rings before his departure. Lance stages a comic farewell with Crab, whose lack of tears troubles him. At Milan, Valentine competes verbally with Thurio and welcomes Proteus warmly. He confides Silvia's love and their planned escape, but Proteus falls for her and decides to betray the elopement to her father, then undermine Thurio. Speed and Lance discuss their masters' affairs. In Verona, Julia commissions a page's disguise from Lucetta and prepares to follow Proteus, trusting his fidelity.

acts.label: ACT III
acts.summary: Proteus informs the Duke that Valentine plans to take Silvia through her window by a rope ladder. Pretending to seek advice about his own courtship, the Duke draws Valentine into describing the method, then discovers the ladder and love letter under his cloak. He banishes him on pain of death. Proteus plays the sympathetic friend, urges departure and offers to carry correspondence. Lance calls his master a knave, then examines a milkmaid's qualifications with Speed, accepting her faults because of her wealth. The Duke and Thurio enlist Proteus to slander Valentine and promote Thurio's suit. Proteus recommends poetry and a nighttime serenade, gaining access for his own designs.

acts.label: ACT IV
acts.summary: Outlaws stop Valentine and Speed, then offer Valentine their leadership. He accepts while forbidding attacks on vulnerable women and poor travellers. Julia arrives disguised as Sebastian and hears Proteus woo Silvia, who rejects his treachery despite his false reports of Julia's and Valentine's deaths. Silvia obtains Eglamour's help to seek Valentine and escape Thurio. Lance recounts Crab's misconduct and his own protective sacrifices; Proteus dismisses him after learning that he substituted Crab for the intended gift dog. Proteus hires Julia and sends her to Silvia with a ring, letter and request for a picture. Silvia rejects the love tokens, sympathises with Julia's suffering and gives the page her portrait and money.

acts.label: ACT V
acts.summary: Silvia escapes with Eglamour, prompting the Duke, Thurio, Proteus and Julia to follow. Outlaws capture her as Eglamour flees. Proteus claims to have rescued her, then threatens to force her when she refuses his love. Valentine intervenes and condemns him. Proteus repents; Valentine forgives him and offers his interest in Silvia, at which Julia swoons. The rings reveal Julia's identity, and Proteus returns to her. Captured by the outlaws, the Duke and Thurio arrive. Thurio abandons Silvia when Valentine threatens him; the Duke approves Valentine and pardons him and his followers. Valentine proposes shared wedding celebrations. Silvia remains silent during these final settlements, and no wedding is staged.
